learningObjective: Understand MetaSchedule: rule-based space expansion, cost model, real measurement.

canonicalClaims.claim: TVM MetaSchedule generates schedule candidates for TensorIR PrimFunc via rule-based space definition, evaluates them with a cost model and real hardware measurement, and iterates to find high-performance implementations.
conditions: Search budget and target hardware are configured.
nonImplications: Does not imply MetaSchedule always beats vendor libraries.

misconceptions.claim: MetaSchedule uses only an analytical cost model with no measurement.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It performs real hardware measurement of top candidates.

misconceptions.claim: MetaSchedule works at the Relax graph level, not TensorIR.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It is a tensor-level (TensorIR PrimFunc) tuner.

misconceptions.claim: MetaSchedule outputs are deterministic given the same PrimFunc and target.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Search seeds and measurement noise affect outcomes.

misconceptions.claim: The search space is a fixed set of templates baked into the compiler.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The space is generated by pluggable schedule rules; template-free (Ansor-style) expansion is a design goal.

implementationFacts: Schedule rules: MultiLevelTiling, InlineSpatial, AutoInline, etc.
Cost models: XGBoost, MLP; measurement drives updates.
